lines.meet: G'day, I'm Liam, firefighter and paramedic back home, healer here. If it all goes bad, stay behind me and breathe out loud so I can hear you.
lines.meet_neighbour: Grom's Rest, mate, I'm in the hut next to the one with the two kids. I'm Liam, and I've seen you about the village.
lines.ask_home: Whereabouts are you from, mate? I'm terrible with accents.
lines.ask_work: What'd you do back home, mate? You've got the look of somebody who's done shifts.
lines.answer_home: Katoomba, up in the Blue Mountains outside Sydney. Gum trees, fog, and a lot of bushfire.
lines.answer_work: Firefighter, then paramedic, then both, for seventeen years. The roster never cared which badge you had on at three in the morning.
lines.chat_food: A barbecue on a Sunday arvo with a cold beer and the crew. Snags, onions, white bread, the whole works.
lines.chat_sleep: A few hours at a time, mate, and up at every noise, same as on call. It does me well enough.
lines.chat_missing: The quiet in the truck on the way back from one that went well. Nobody says anything, and everybody's grinning.
lines.chat_here: My first year here was the easiest of my life, because the job was everywhere. Then it went quiet for a season, and that nearly finished me.
lines.tease_quiet: You're like a good crew member, {name}, never says a word and always turns up, and I love it.
lines.tease_talker: Mate, {name}, you'd talk a cocky off a branch. Keep going, I'm enjoying it.
lines.tease_careful: You size up a job like an old fire chief, {name}. Good on you, mate, but we're losing the light.
lines.tease_bold: You'd run into a burning shed for a cat, {name}. I know, because I would too.
lines.tease_any: You'd be all right on my crew, {name}, if you could make a decent cuppa. Work on it.
lines.tease_back: Fair cop, {name}, that one landed, mate.
lines.take_it_kindly: Too right, {name}, I can't argue with that one.
lines.bristle: Nah, leave that one, {name}. It's not a joking thing for me.
lines.apologise: Sorry, mate, that came out wrong. I'm tired, and I took it out on you.
lines.double_down: I'll stand by that one, mate. Somebody had to say it.
lines.needle_quiet: You freeze up and say nothing when it matters. I need to know where you are, mate.
lines.needle_talker: Mate, calm down and stop talking for a sec. Panic's catching, and you're spreading it.
lines.needle_careful: You stand in the doorway thinking while it all burns. Move, or get out of the way.
lines.needle_bold: You go in alone every time, and I know exactly where that ends up, mate.
lines.needle_any: You panic, every time, and somebody else has to deal with it, usually me.
lines.bite_back: I've carried people out of burning houses, mate. Don't tell me I don't pull my weight.
lines.hurt: Yeah, that one stung, I'll be honest. I'll go and have a cuppa and think on it.
lines.laugh_off: Mate, I've had drunks on the highway at three in the morning say worse. Water off a duck's back.
lines.confide: {name}, I lost two of my crew in the 2019 fires, and half my street, and I went straight back to work. I never stopped to look at it.
lines.listen: No rush, {name}, mate. I'm here, and it stays with me.
lines.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}, and breathe out loud so I can hear you.
lines.accept: No worries, {name}, I'll do it your way, mate.
lines.deflect: She'll be right, {name}, it's a scratch from the highway days. Help someone worse off.
lines.check_in: Breathe out loud for me, {name}, so I can hear it. Where's it hurting?
lines.blame: Going in alone, in there, and the rest of us paid for it. I know the look, mate.
lines.thank: Mate, you got me back, and I'm usually the one doing that. I owe you a beer, a big one.
lines.brush_off: No worries, mate, that's the job. Breathe slow, you're right.
lines.worry: Steady, {name}, steady, I've got you. Breathe out loud for me.
lines.handed_down: Reckon this was yours, mate. You'll get it back, no dramas.
lines.hand_fine: No worries, it's yours, mate. I've got my shears, that's plenty.
lines.hand_sulk: Bit rough, nobody asking. I'll get over it.
lines.turn_friendly: You're one of my crew now, {name}, mate. That's the best thing I can say about anybody.
lines.turn_friends: I'd go in for you, {name}, any fire, any night. And I'd let you go in for me, which is harder.
lines.turn_grating: We don't really click, mate. No worries, we'll get the job done.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still pull you out if it comes to it, mate, that's who I am. Don't expect a barbie after.
lines.make_up: Righto, {name}, let's knock this on the head, mate. Reckon we can start again?
lines.defend: Oi, ease up, mate, that's not on. {name} did everything right.
lines.friend_left: It's a quiet station without {name}. I keep listening for the radio.
lines.friend_back: Good on you, {name}, you're back! Crew's complete again, mate.
lines.common_medic: Seventeen years as a paramedic, mostly at three in the morning on the highway. Anyone who's worked in medicine knows the worst calls come at the worst hours.
lines.common_fire_crew: I fought bushfires for seventeen summers in the Blue Mountains. Anybody who's been on a fire line knows you watch the wind before you watch the fire.
lines.common_rescue: Going back in for people is the whole job, mate. Somebody who's done rescue work has that same look, like they're always counting heads.
lines.common_aussie: You're an Aussie! Mate, where from? I haven't heard a proper accent in years.
